name: Computer Science, M.S.
college: College of Engineering and Computing Sciences
source_notes: 30 credits total. Fundamental (9) + System Programming pick 2 (6) + Application pick 2 (6) + Project/Thesis (3-6) + Electives (3-6). Graduate courses generally require admitted graduate standing; specific course-level prereqs are department-approved.

requirement_blocks.name: Project or Thesis Track
requirement_blocks.notes: Thesis: CSCI 890 + CSCI 891 (6 cr). Non-thesis: 3-cr project + 3 additional electives.

requirement_blocks.name: Electives
requirement_blocks.notes: 3 credits for thesis track, 6 credits for non-thesis track.

courses.title: Theoretical Concepts in Computers and Computation
courses.description: Formal languages, automata, computability, and complexity theory at the graduate level.

courses.title: Computer Architecture I
courses.description: Advanced computer architecture — pipelining, caches, memory hierarchies.

courses.title: Operating System Security
courses.description: Secure OS design, access control, and hardening.

courses.title: Programming Languages
courses.description: Programming language paradigms, formal semantics, and type systems.

courses.title: Compiler Theory I
courses.description: Compiler design — lexical/syntax analysis, code generation, optimization.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Advanced software engineering methodologies and practices.

courses.title: Computer Graphics
courses.description: 3D graphics, rendering pipelines, and shader programming.

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: Graduate-level computer networking — protocols, architectures, and performance.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence I
courses.description: Graduate-level AI — search, knowledge representation, planning, and introduction to ML.

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.description: Graduate-level database systems, query processing, and transaction management.

courses.title: MS Thesis I
courses.description: First semester of MS thesis research.

courses.title: MS Thesis II
courses.description: Second semester of MS thesis — defense.
